title: Temurah 29
description: The end of Rabbi Abba bar Kahana’s list of what was permitted to Gideon, the source and limits of “set-aside,” why set-aside and worshipped animals may still be eaten while a tereifa needs three verses, and the mishna and Gemara on a prostitute’s payment: a hundred lambs for one, payment given before or after, Rav and Levi on a menstruating wife, and Abaye and Rava on a gentile and a Jewish prostitute.
topics: 🪓 Gideon’s night: service vessels, the asheira’s vessels and wood, set-aside and worshipped
🛡️ “You shall safeguard it… to Me”: Rabbi Yoshiya’s source for set-aside, and Abaye’s weak lamb
⏳ Until when is it set aside? Work, the attendants, vetches, shearing; and Baha, “from here and there”
🍽️ Set-aside and worshipped may be eaten; three verses for the tereifa
🐑 Mishna: a prostitute’s payment, a hundred lambs, and the slave and the maidservant
⏱️ Given before, given after, sacrificed first: Rabbi Elazar, Rav Oshaya’s unresolved dilemma, Rav Ḥanan bar Rav Ḥisda
⚖️ Rav and Levi on a menstruating wife; Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi on payment a woman gives a man
📜 Abaye and Rava on a gentile and a Jewish prostitute, Rabbi Akiva on betrothal, and a widow with a High Priest

a1.he: וּכְלִי שָׁרֵת, וּכְלִי אֲשֵׁירָה, וַעֲצֵי אֲשֵׁירָה, וּמוּקְצֶה, וְנֶעֱבָד.

a2.he: אָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר מַתְנָה, אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה: מִנַּיִן לְמוּקְצֶה מִן הַתּוֹרָה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״תִּשְׁמְרוּ לְהַקְרִיב לִי בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ״ — כֹּל שֶׁעוֹשִׂין לוֹ שִׁימּוּר.

a3.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ אַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, (אייתית) [אַיְיתִי] אִימְּרָא דְּצוֹמָא, וְלָא עָבֵיד לֵיהּ שִׁימּוּר, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא חֲזֵי לְהַקְרָבָה? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא ״תִּשְׁמְרוּ לְהַקְרִיב לִי בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ״ קָאָמֵינָא — ״לִי״ וְלֹא לְאָדוֹן אַחֵר, וְאֵיזֶהוּ אַחֵר שֶׁמַּקְרִיבִין לוֹ? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זוֹ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.

a4.he: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק: אֵין מוּקְצֶה אָסוּר אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁיַּעַבְדוּ [בּוֹ]. עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עַד שֶׁיִּמְסְרוּהוּ לְכוּמְרֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.

a5.he: בָּהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עַד שֶׁיַּאֲכִילוּהוּ כַּרְשִׁינֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְבָהָא: מִפַּלְגִיתוּ אַתּוּן אַעוּלָּא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, עוּלָּא נָמֵי כִּי קָאָמַר — הוּא דְּשָׁפֵי לֵיהּ כַּרְשִׁינֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.

a6.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: יָדַע בְּהָא לְשַׁנּוֹיֵי שְׁמַעְתָּא, וְאִי לָא דְּסָלֵיק הָתָם — לָא הֲוָה יָדַע, דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל גְּרַמָה לֵיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יִצְחָק: בָּהָא מִיכָּן וּמִיכָּן הֲוָה.

a7.he: דְּתָנֵי רַב חֲנַנְיָא טְרִיטָאָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין מוּקְצֶה אָסוּר אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁיַּעֲשׂוּ בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה, הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ (וַהֲדַר) [וְהוּא] אָמַר לַהּ: מַאי ״מַעֲשֶׂה״? — עַד שֶׁיִּגָּזֵז וְיַעַבְדוּ בּוֹ.

a8.he: אֵיזֶהוּ נֶעֱבָד כּוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי?

a9.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״מִמַּשְׁקֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל״, מִן הַמּוּתָּר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אֲסִירִי לְהֶדְיוֹט, לְמָה לִי קְרָא (מעטינהו) [לְמַעֹטִינְהוּ] מִגָּבוֹהַּ?

a10.he: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דַּאֲסִירִי לְהֶדְיוֹט — לָא בָּעֵי קְרָא? וְהָא טְרֵפָה, דַּאֲסִירָא לְהֶדְיוֹט, וּמַעֲטֵיהּ קָרָא מִגָּבוֹהַּ!

a11.he: דְּתַנְיָא: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״מִן הַבָּקָר״ לְמַטָּה, שֶׁאֵין תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר, אֶלָּא לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַטְּרֵפָה.

a12.he: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אֲמִינָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי — דְּנִטְרְפָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְקַדְּשָׁה, אֲבָל נִתְקַדְּשָׁה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְרְפָה — אֵימָא (דתישרי) [דְּתִישְׁתְּרֵי] לְגָבוֹהַּ.

a13.he: וְהָא מֵהָכָא נָפְקָא, ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבוֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט״, פְּרָט לִטְרֵפָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ עוֹבֶרֶת.

a14.he: הָהוּא נָמֵי אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר, דְּנוֹלְדָה טְרֵפָה מִמְּעֵי אִמָּהּ, אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר, וְיָצָאת לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִטְרְפָה — אֵימָא תִּשְׁתְּרֵי לְגָבוֹהַּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a15.he: מַתְנִי׳ וְאֵיזֶהוּ אֶתְנַן? — הָאוֹמֵר לְזוֹנָה ״הֵולִיךְ טָלֶה זֶה בִּשְׂכָרֵךְ״, אֲפִילּוּ הֵן מֵאָה, כּוּלָּן אֲסוּרִין. וְכֵן הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ ״הֵולָיךְ טָלֶה זֶה וְתָלִין שִׁפְחָתְךָ אֵצֶל עַבְדִּי״ — רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ אֶתְנַן, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֶתְנַן.

a16.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר מָר: וַאֲפִילּוּ הֵן מֵאָה, כּוּלָּן אֲסוּרִין. הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּשָׁקְלָה אַגְרַאּ מֵאָה בְּהֵמוֹת — פְּשִׁיטָא דְּכוּלְּהוּ אֲסִירִי, מָה לִי חַד, מָה לִי מְאָה!

a17.he: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּשָׁקְלָה אַגְרַאּ חֲדָא, וְיָהֵיב לַהּ מְאָה, דְּכוּלְּהוּ מִכֹּחַ אֶתְנַן קָאָתוּ.

a18.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נָתַן לָהּ וְלֹא בָּא עָלֶיהָ, בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְלֹא נָתַן לָהּ — אֶתְנַנָּה מוּתָּר. נָתַן לָהּ וְלֹא בָּא עָלֶיהָ, ״אֶתְנַנָּה״ קָרֵית לֵיהּ? וְתוּ, בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְלֹא נָתַן לָהּ, מַאי יָהֵיב לַהּ?

a19.he: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָתָנֵי: נָתַן לָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא עָלֶיהָ; בָּא עָלֶיהָ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָתַן לָהּ — אֶתְנַנָּה מוּתָּר. וְלֵיחוּל עֲלֵיהּ אֶתְנַן לְמַפְרֵעַ? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:

b1.he: שֶׁקָּדְמָה וְהִקְרִיבַתּוּ. הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי נֵימָא דְּאַקְנְיֵהּ נִיהֲלַיהּ לְאַלְתַּר — פְּשִׁיטָא דְּמוּתָּר, דְּעַד כָּאן לֹא בָּא עָלֶיהָ!

b2.he: וְאֶלָּא, דַּאֲמַר לַהּ: ״לָא נִיקְּנֵי לִיךְ עַד שְׁעַת בִּיאָה״, מִי מָצְיָא מַקְרְבָה לֵיהּ? ״אִישׁ כִּי יַקְדִּישׁ אֶת בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳״ אֲמַר רַחֲמָנָא, מָה בֵּיתוֹ בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ, אַף כֹּל בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ!

b3.he: לָא צְרִיכָא, דַּאֲמַר לַהּ: ״לָא (מִקַּנְיָה) [נִיקְּנֵי] לָךְ עַד שְׁעַת בִּיאָה, וְאִי מִצְטְרִיךְ לָךְ נִיקְּנֵי לָךְ מֵעַכְשָׁיו״.

b4.he: בָּעֵי רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: קָדְמָה וְהִקְדִּישַׁתּוּ, מַאי? תִּפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: קָדְמָה וְהִקְרִיבַתּוּ. הִקְרִיבַתּוּ הִיא דְּהָא לֵיתֵיהּ בִּשְׁעַת בִּיאָה, אֲבָל הִקְדִּישַׁתּוּ — אָסוּר!

b5.he: הִיא גּוּפַהּ קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ: הִקְרִיבַתּוּ, (וְהָא) [דְּהָא] לֵיתֵיהּ בִּשְׁעַת בִּיאָה — מוּתָּר, אֲבָל הִקְדִּישַׁתּוּ בִּשְׁעַת בִּיאָה — אָסוּר.

b6.he: אוֹ דִּלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דִּתְנַן ״אֲמִירָתוֹ לַגָּבוֹהַּ כִּמְסִירָתוֹ לְהֶדְיוֹט״, הִקְדִּישַׁתּוּ מוּתָּר, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן הִקְרִיבַתּוּ? תֵּיקוּ.

b7.he: בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָתַן לָהּ אֶתְנַנָּה — מוּתָּר, וְהָתַנְיָא: בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְנָתַן לָהּ, וַאֲפִילּוּ עַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ — אֶתְנַנָּה אָסוּר!

b8.he: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאָמַר לַהּ ״הִבָּעֲלִי לִי בְּטָלֶה זֶה״, הָא דְּאָמַר לַהּ ״הִבָּעֲלִי לִי בְּטָלֶה״ סְתָם.

b9.he: ״טָלֶה זֶה״, וְהָא מְחוּסַּר מְשִׁיכָה! בְּזוֹנָה גּוֹיָה, דְּלָא קָנְיָא בִּמְשִׁיכָה. וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: אֲפִילּוּ בְּזוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית, כְּגוֹן דְּקָאֵי בַּחֲצֵרַהּ.

b10.he: הָא יַהֲבֵיהּ לַהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא, דְּשַׁוְּויֵהּ לַהּ אַפּוֹתֵיקֵי, וַאֲמַר לַהּ: ״אִם עַד יוֹם פְּלוֹנִי יָהֵיבְנָא לָךְ זוּזֵי — מוּטָב, וְאִם לָאו — טָלֶה בְּאֶתְנַנִּךְ״.

b11.he: אָמַר רַב: אֶחָד אֶתְנַן זָכָר, וְאֶחָד אֶתְנַן כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת אָסוּר, חוּץ מֵאֶתְנַן אִשְׁתּוֹ נִדָּה.

b12.he: מַאי טַעְמָא? ״זוֹנָה״ כְּתִיב, וְהָא לָאו זוֹנָה הִיא.

b13.he: וְלֵוִי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ אִשְׁתּוֹ נִדָּה. מַאי טַעְמָא? ״תּוֹעֵבָה״ כְּתִיב, וְהָא תּוֹעֵבָה הִיא.

b14.he: וְלֵוִי נָמֵי, וְהָכְתִיב ״זוֹנָה״! אָמַר לָךְ: הָהִיא ״זוֹנָה״, וְלֹא זוֹנֶה. וְרַב, הָהִיא זוֹנָה וְלֹא זוֹנֶה מְנָא לֵיהּ?

b15.he: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֵין אֶתְנַן אָסוּר אֶלָּא (כׇּל) אֶתְנַן [כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת] הַבָּאוֹת לוֹ בַּעֲבֵירָה, אֲבָל אֶתְנַן אִשְׁתּוֹ נִדָּה, וְשֶׁנָּתַן לָהּ שָׂכָר לְהַפְקָעָתָהּ, וְשֶׁנָּתְנָה לוֹ [הִיא] בְּאֶתְנַנּוֹ — מוּתָּרִין.

b16.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר, זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר: ״וּבְתִתֵּךְ אֶתְנָן וְאֶתְנַן לֹא נִיתַּן [לָךְ] (לָהּ) וַתְּהִי לְהֶפֶךְ״.

b17.he: וְרַב, הַאי ״תּוֹעֵבָה״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ כִּדְאַבָּיֵי, דְּאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: זוֹנָה גּוֹיָה — אֶתְנַנָּה אָסוּר.

b18.he: מַאי טַעְמָא? כְּתִיב הָכָא ״תּוֹעֵבָה״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם ״כִּי כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה מִכֹּל הַתּוֹעֵבוֹת הָאֵל״, מָה לְהַלָּן עֲרָיוֹת שֶׁאֵין קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בָּהּ, הָכִי נָמֵי אֵין קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בָּהּ.

b19.he: וְכֹהֵן שֶׁבָּא עָלֶיהָ — אֵין לוֹקֶה עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם זוֹנָה, מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״לֹא יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ״ — מִי שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ מְיוּחָס אַחֲרָיו, יָצָא גּוֹיָה דְּאֵין זַרְעוֹ מְיוּחָס אַחֲרָיו.

b20.he: זוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית — אֶתְנַנָּה מוּתָּר, מָה טַעַם? דְּהָא קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בָּהּ, וְכֹהֵן שֶׁבָּא עָלֶיהָ — לוֹקֶה מִשּׁוּם זוֹנָה, מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּהָא זַרְעוֹ מְיוּחָס אַחֲרָיו.

b21.he: וְרָבָא אָמַר: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה, אֶתְנַנָּה אָסוּר, וְכֹהֵן הַבָּא עָלֶיהָ לוֹקֶה מִשּׁוּם זוֹנָה. מַאי טַעְמָא? יָלְפִי מֵהֲדָדֵי — מָה זוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית בְּלָאו, אַף זוֹנָה גּוֹיָה בְּלָאו, וּמָה אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה גּוֹיָה אָסוּר, אַף אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית אָסוּר.

b22.he: מֵיתִיבִי: אֶחָד זוֹנָה גּוֹיָה וְאֶחָד זוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית — אֶתְנַנָּה אָסוּר. תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּאַבָּיֵי! אָמַר לָךְ אַבָּיֵי: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, דְּאָמַר: אֵין קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בְּחַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין.

b23.he: וְהָא קָמַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּכׇל זוֹנָה לָא תָּפְסִי בַּהּ קִדּוּשִׁין, דּוּמְיָא דְּאַלְמָנָה דְּלָא תָּפְסִי בַּהּ קִידּוּשִׁין.

b24.he: וּלְרָבָא, מַאי שְׁנָא דְּקָתָנֵי ״כְּגוֹן אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל״? דּוּמְיָא דְּאַלְמָנָה — מָה אַלְמָנָה לָא לָקֵי עַד דְּמַתְרִי בֵּהּ, אַף זוֹנָה — עַד דְּאָמַר ״הֵא לִךָ״.

b25.he: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: פָּנוּי הַבָּא עַל פְּנוּיָה שֶׁלֹּא לְשֵׁם אִישׁוּת — עֲשָׂאָהּ זוֹנָה, אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּזוֹנָה מֵעִיקָּרָא — הָכִי נָמֵי דְּאָסוּר.

b26.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחְרִינָא: כִּי קָתָנֵי הָא — בַּעֲרָיוֹת שֶׁאֵין קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בָּהּ.

b27.he: וְהָא קָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, גְּרוּשָׁה וַחֲלוּצָה לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט — אֶתְנַנָּה אָסוּר, וְהָא הָנֵי קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בָּהֶן! הָא מַנִּי?

messages.text: Continued from 28b: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana says that eight prohibited matters were permitted to Gideon on the night he destroyed his father’s idolatry: slaughtering sacrificial animals outside the Tabernacle, sacrificing at night, and service by non-priests;

and the prohibition against sacrificing without service vessels; and the prohibition against utilizing vessels that had been previously used for the service of a tree worshipped as idolatry [asheira]; and the prohibition against using the wood of an asheira, as God commanded Gideon to sacrifice the burnt offering with the wood of an asheira that he will cut down (Judges 6:26); and the prohibition of sacrificing an animal set aside for idolatry; and the prohibition against using an animal that was worshipped as an idol.

notes.he: כלומר שלא הוצרך לכלי שרת:
notes.en: And service vessels: that is, he did not need service vessels.

notes.he: שהקריב בכלי אשירה באותו שהיה משמש לאשירה שימש לשם:
notes.en: And vessels of an asheira: he sacrificed with the vessels of the asheira, those same vessels that had served the asheira he used there.

notes.he: הקטירו דכתיב התם ואת האשירה אשר עליה תכרות:
notes.en: And with the wood of an asheira: he burned it [the offering], as it is written there: “And the asheira that is by it you shall cut down” [Judges 6:25].

notes.he: הקטירו:
notes.en: And with the wood of an asheira: he burned it [the offering].

notes.he: היה אבל בעלמא כל מוקצה סתם לעבודת כוכבים הוי מוקצה ואסור:
notes.en: And set-aside and worshipped: [Gideon’s bull] was [both]. But in general, any animal set aside without further specification for idol worship is set-aside and prohibited.

messages.text: From where is the halakha of set-aside derived in the Torah? As it is stated with regard to the offerings: “My food that is presented to Me for offerings made by fire, of a pleasing aroma to Me, you shall safeguard it to sacrifice to Me in its due season” (Numbers 28:2), which refers to anything that is safeguarded.
messages.lead: § The Gemara continues to discuss the halakha of an animal set aside for idol worship.

verse.he: צַו אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אֶת־קׇרְבָּנִי לַחְמִי לְאִשַּׁי רֵיחַ נִיחֹחִי תִּשְׁמְרוּ לְהַקְרִיב לִי בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ׃
verse.en: Command the Israelite people and say to them: Be punctilious in presenting to Me at stated times the offerings of food due Me, as offerings by fire of pleasing odor to Me.

notes.he: קס"ד דהכי קאמר מנין שחייב אדם להקצות קרבנו לשמים ולא יקריבנו מיד כשהקדישו:
notes.en: From where is set-aside derived in the Torah: it initially enters our mind that this is what he means: From where do we learn that a person must set aside his offering for Heaven, and not sacrifice it immediately when he has consecrated it?

notes.he: לתורת גבוה:
notes.en: Safeguarding: for the purposes of the Most High.

notes.he: קא סלקא דעתך דהכי קאמר מנין שצריך להקצות הקרבן לשם הקרבה לגבוה קודם ההקרבה ומסיק דקאמר מנין דאסור להקריב אותו שהוקצה לעבודת כוכבים וקצת קשה דהא דרשינן מקראי אחריני טובא והיה לו לומר הך תנא מייתי ליה מהכא:
notes.en: From where is set-aside (prohibited) in the Torah: it initially enters our mind that this is what he means: From where do we learn that one must set aside the offering for the sake of sacrifice to the Most High before it is sacrificed? And he concludes that he means: From where do we learn that it is forbidden to sacrifice an animal that was set aside for idol worship? And this is somewhat difficult, since we derive this from many other verses; he should have said: This tanna brings it from here.

notes.he: מנין למוקצה מן התורה שצריך להקצותו ולעשות לו שימור קודם הקרבה דכתיב תשמרו להקריב לי:
notes.en: From where is set-aside derived in the Torah: that one must set it aside and safeguard it before it is sacrificed, as it is written: “You shall safeguard to sacrifice to Me.”

notes.he: [לפניו] (לפטמו):
notes.en: Anything for which they provide safeguarding: [before it is sacrificed], (to fatten it).

messages.text: The Gemara initially assumes that Rabbi Yoshiya meant that any sacrifice must be safeguarded, i.e., set aside and not sacrificed immediately after its consecration.

If that is so, then in a case where one brought a lamb that was weak as an offering, and its owner clearly did not safeguard it, so too will you say that it is unfit for sacrifice? Nowhere is it stated that an animal is disqualified for the altar because it has not been treated well.
messages.quote: which refers to anything that is safeguarded

notes.he: כבש רעב שלא נשמר מעולם ולא חששו:
notes.en: A hungry lamb [imra detzoma]: a hungry lamb that was never safeguarded, and they paid no attention to it.

notes.he: פלח אימרא דצומא דלא עבד שימור כלומר אם הקריב כבש כחוש שלא נעשה לו שימור שאינו מפוטם הכי נמי דאסורה:
notes.en: If that is so, one who brought a hungry lamb and did not safeguard it: that is, if he sacrificed a lean lamb for which no safeguarding was done, since it was not fattened, would it also be prohibited?

messages.text: You misunderstood my intention; I say that the verse: “You shall safeguard it to sacrifice to Me in its due season,” should be interpreted as follows: You shall safeguard it only for Me, but not to another master. And which is this other master to which one could sacrifice? You must say that this is an object of idol worship.

notes.he: דהכי קאמינא למוקצה לעבודת כוכבים שאסור מן התורה מהכא:
notes.en: For Me, and not for another master: for this is what I meant: that an animal set aside for idol worship is prohibited by Torah law is derived from here.

notes.dh: א"ל אנא תשמרו להקריב לי במועדו קאמינא
notes.he: כל שמוקצה לגבוה ולא לאדון אחר:
notes.en: He said to him: I am speaking of “You shall safeguard it to sacrifice to Me in its due season”: anything that is set aside for the Most High, and not for another master.

messages.text: An animal that has been set aside for idol worship is prohibited, i.e., still considered set aside, only until it has been used for work by the attendants of that idolatry. But once it has been used it is no longer prohibited, as it will not be sacrificed to the idol afterward.
messages.lead: The Gemara continues to discuss the definition of an animal that has been set aside for idolatry.

notes.he: בו שום עבודה לצורך עבודת כוכבים או משיכת קרון או שום דבר שאסור אבל מקמי הכי לא מיתסר. ל"א אין מוקצה אסור אלא עד שיעבדו בו שום דבר שיעשו בו שום עבודה לצורך כומרי עבודת כוכבים אבל משיעבדו בו שום עבודה לא מיתסר דתו לא מקרבי ליה וכ"ש ולשון זה נראה לי עיקר מדתני אלא עד שיעבדו בו ואי ללישנא קמא לא ה"ל למיתני אלא והכי איבעי ליה למיתני אין מוקצה אסור עד שיעבדו בו ולשון ראשון ל"ש:
notes.en: Until they work with it: until they do some work with it for the sake of idol worship, or pulling a wagon, or anything that is forbidden; but before that, it is not prohibited. Another version: set-aside is prohibited only until they do something with it, some work for the needs of the priests of idol worship; but once they have done some work with it, it is not prohibited, since they will no longer sacrifice it. [The text has here “and all the more so”; Tosafot, quoting this Rashi, reads “so I heard.”] And this version seems to me the main one, since it teaches “only until they work with it.” According to the first version it should not have taught “only”; it should have taught: Set-aside is not prohibited until they work with it. And the first version I did not hear [from my teachers].

notes.he: פרש"י שיעבדו בו שום עבודה לשם עבודת כוכבים או משיכת קרון או שום דבר האיסור אבל מקמי הכי לא מיתסרי ל"א עד שיעבדו בו שום עבודה לצורך הכומרים אבל (אם) משיעבדו בו שום עבודה לצורך הכומרים לא מיתסר דתו לא מיקרבי כך שמעתי ולשון זה נראה לי עיקר מדתני אלא עד שיעבדו כו' ואי כלישנא קמא (לא) הוה מצי למיתני אין מוקצה אסור (אלא) עד שיעבדו ולשון ראשון לא שמעתי ל' רש"י:
notes.en: Only until they work, etc.: Rashi explained: until they do some work with it for the sake of idol worship, or pulling a wagon, or anything forbidden; but before that they are not prohibited. Another version: until they do some work with it for the needs of the priests; but once they have done some work with it for the needs of the priests, it is not prohibited, since they will no longer sacrifice it. So I heard. And this version seems to me the main one, since it teaches “only until they work, etc.”; according to the first version he could have taught: Set-aside is prohibited [only] once they work with it. And the first version I did not hear. [This is] Rashi’s wording.

messages.text: An animal that has been set aside for idol worship is prohibited only until it has been handed over to the attendants of idol worship for fattening for it to be eaten, even if it has not been used for any form of work. But after it has been handed over it is not prohibited, as it will not be sacrificed.

notes.he: לאכילה דתו לא מקרבי ליה:
notes.en: Until they hand it over to the priests: for eating; after that they will no longer sacrifice it.

messages.text: A set-aside animal is prohibited only until its owner feeds it vetches of idolatry after it has been given to the attendants of idolatry.

notes.he: שמפטמין אותו לצורך הכומרים ותו לא מקרבי ליה:
notes.en: Until they feed it vetches of idol worship: with which they fatten it for the needs of the priests, and after that they will no longer sacrifice it.

messages.text: @Baha Do you dispute the statement of Ulla, who defined set-aside differently according the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan?
messages.quote: until its owner feeds it vetches of idolatry

messages.text: No, I do not disagree with Ulla, as Ulla too, when he stated his definition, also was referring to a case where they fed it vetches of idolatry.
Baha knows how to explain this halakha, but had he not ascended from Babylonia to there, Eretz Yisrael, he would not have known this explanation, as Eretz Yisrael caused him to grow wise.
@Rabbi Abba That is not the case, as Baha was from here and there, i.e., he became wise because he studied Torah in both places.
messages.quote: had he not ascended from Babylonia to there, Eretz Yisrael, he would not have known

notes.he: מבבל ומארץ ישראל:
notes.en: He was from here and from there: from Babylonia and from the Land of Israel.

notes.he: פירוש בהא מארץ ישראל ומבבל היה תלמיד חכם ולא מהניא זכותא דארץ ישראל:
notes.en: Baha was from here and from there: meaning, Baha was a Torah scholar from the Land of Israel and from Babylonia, and it was not the merit of the Land of Israel that helped him.

notes.he: כלומר כבר ידע באתא לשנויי שמעתא וזה הועיל לו דסליק להתם דאויר דא"י מחכים. א"ל רב נחמן באתא ודאי ידע לתרוצי דמיכן ומיכן הוה ולמד בין בבבל בין בא"י:
notes.en: Baha knows: that is, Baha already knew how to explain the teaching, and what helped him was that he went up there, for the air of the Land of Israel makes one wise. Rav Naḥman [so Rabbeinu Gershom’s text; the printed Gemara has Rav Yitzḥak] said to him: Baha certainly knew how to answer, for he was from here and from there, and he studied both in Babylonia and in the Land of Israel.

messages.text: An animal that has been set aside for idolatry is prohibited only until an action has been performed upon it.
messages.lead: The Gemara continues to discuss the issue of set-aside. Rabbi Ḥananya Terita taught before Rabbi Yoḥanan:

messages.text: What is the meaning of an action? It means until it is sheared and used for labor by the attendants of the idol.
messages.lead: He taught it and then said its explanation:

notes.dh: אלא עד שיעשו בו מעשה לשם עבודת כוכבים
notes.he: כלומר או גיזה או עבודה:
notes.en: Only until they perform an action upon it for the sake of idol worship: that is, either shearing or labor.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: Which is the animal that is worshipped as idolatry? It is any animal that one worships. The mishna proceeds to state: The consumption of both this, the animal designated for idol worship, and that, the animal worshipped, is permitted.
From where are these matters derived?

notes.he: דמותרין לאכילה להדיוט:
notes.en: From where are these matters derived: that they are permitted for an ordinary person to eat.

notes.dh: מנא ה"מ שמותר מוקצה ונעבד להדיוט
notes.he: תימה מהיכא תיתי לאסור להדיוט דהא אפי' לגבוה לא מיתסר אי לאו הני קראי דלעיל להדיוט מהיכא תיתי לאסור ואומר ר"י דכיון דמפיק מקרא דאסור לגבוה אף להדיוט נילף מינה דאסור ואי קשיא א"כ מאי קא משני אי סלקא דעתך אסורין להדיוט למה לי קרא למעוטי לגבוה הא לא מיתסר להדיוט אלא מקרא דגבוה ויש לומר דהכי קאמר אי ס"ד דגמרינן איסור להדיוט מקרא דשמעינן מיניה איסור לגבוה למה לי למיכתביה לאיסור גבי קרבנות לכתביה גבי הדיוט וממילא ידעינן דאסור לגבוה ממשקה ישראל מן המותר לישראל:
notes.en: From where are these matters derived, that set-aside and worshipped are permitted to an ordinary person: this is puzzling. From where would one come to prohibit them to an ordinary person? Even for the Most High they would not be prohibited were it not for those verses above; from where would one come to prohibit them to an ordinary person? And the Ri says: since he derives from a verse that they are prohibited for the Most High, let us derive from it that they are prohibited to an ordinary person as well. And if it is difficult: if so, what is the answer “If it enters your mind that they are prohibited to an ordinary person, why do I need a verse to exclude them from the Most High?” They would be prohibited to an ordinary person only by virtue of the verse about the Most High! One may say that this is what he means: If it enters your mind that we derive a prohibition for an ordinary person from a verse from which we learn a prohibition for the Most High, why do I need the prohibition to be written with regard to offerings? Let it be written with regard to the ordinary person, and we would automatically know that it is prohibited for the Most High from “the well-watered pastures of Israel,” from what is permitted to Israel.

notes.he: דמותרין באכילה מדאיצטריך קרא למעוטי ממשקה ישראל היינו מן המותר לישראל יהא ראוי להקרב כלומר דהני אע"ג דמותר באכילה אסור לגבוה דהא כתיב מן הבקר ומן הצאן למעוטי מוקצה ונעבד:
notes.en: From where are these matters derived: that they are permitted to eat, since a verse was needed to exclude them. “From the well-watered pastures of Israel” means: from what is permitted to Israel shall be fit to be sacrificed. That is, these, even though they are permitted to eat, are prohibited to the Most High, for it is written “from the herd and from the flock” to exclude set-aside and worshipped.

messages.text: “And one lamb of the flock, out of two hundred, from the well-watered pastures of Israel, for a meal offering, and for a burnt offering, and for peace offerings, to make atonement for them” (Ezekiel 45:15). The expression: “From the well-watered pastures of Israel,” means that one brings offerings only from that which is permitted to Israel.
messages.lead: Rav Pappa said that the verse states, with regard to offerings:

verse.he: וְשֶׂה־אַחַת מִן־הַצֹּאן מִן־הַמָּאתַיִם מִמַּשְׁקֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמִנְחָה וּלְעוֹלָה וְלִשְׁלָמִים לְכַפֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם נְאֻם אֲדֹנָי יֱהֹוִה׃ {פ}
verse.en: And [the due] from the flock shall be one animal from every 200. [All these shall be contributed] from Israel’s products for grain offerings, burnt offerings, and offerings of well-being, to make expiation for them—declares the Sovereign GOD.

notes.he: גבי קרבנות כתיב במשכנא דיחזקאל. משמע מן המותר לאכילת ישראל הבא קרבן:
notes.en: From the well-watered pastures of Israel: it is written with regard to offerings, in Ezekiel’s [account of the] Temple. It implies: from what is permitted for Israel to eat, bring an offering.

messages.text: And if it enters your mind that a set-aside animal and one worshipped as idolatry are prohibited in consumption to an ordinary person, why do I need a verse to exclude them from sacrifice to the Most High, as that would be obvious. Rather, they must be permitted in consumption to an ordinary person.

notes.he: דמוקצה ונעבד אסירי להדיוט ל"ל הני קראי דלעיל מן הבקר להוציא את הנעבד מן הצאן להוציא את המוקצה ממשקה ישראל נפקא דמשאסור להדיוט אסור לגבוה:
notes.en: And if it enters your mind: that set-aside and worshipped are prohibited to an ordinary person, why do I need those verses above, “from the herd” to exclude the worshipped, “from the flock” to exclude the set-aside? It would be derived from “the well-watered pastures of Israel,” since once something is prohibited to an ordinary person, it is prohibited to the Most High.

notes.he: באכילה א"כ ל"ל קרא מן הבקר ומן הצאן למעוטי תיפוק לי ממשקה מן המותר לישראל אלא ש"מ להכי איצטריך קרא למעוטי משום דמותר באכילה וכל היכא וכו']:
notes.en: For if it enters your mind that they are prohibited to an ordinary person: to eat, then why do I need the verse “from the herd and from the flock” to exclude them? Derive it from “the well-watered pastures,” from what is permitted to Israel! Rather, learn from this that the verse was needed to exclude them because they are permitted to eat. And anywhere, etc.

notes.he: ל"א אי אמרת בשלמא שרי לישראל באכילה [מוקצה ונעבד] היינו דצריך קרא מן הבקר ומן הצאן למעוטינהו לגבוה אע"ג דשרו לישראל אלא אי אמרת כו'. [והיינו] כלישנא קמא אלא דבהאי [לישנא] מפורש טפי:
notes.en: Another version: Granted, if you say that [set-aside and worshipped] are permitted to Israel to eat, that is why a verse, “from the herd and from the flock,” is needed to exclude them for the Most High, even though they are permitted to Israel. But if you say, etc. [This is] like the first version, but in this version it is spelled out more fully.

messages.text: And is it true that anywhere that an item is prohibited to an ordinary person, a verse is not necessary to teach that it may not be used as a sacrifice? But there is the case of an animal with a condition that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa], which is prohibited in consumption to an ordinary person, and yet a verse excludes it from sacrifice to the Most High.
messages.quote: why do I need a verse to exclude them from sacrifice to the Most High

messages.text: It was previously derived from the verse: “You shall bring your offering from the cattle, even from the herd or from the flock” (Leviticus 1:2), that certain animals are prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar (see 28a). When it says below, in the next verse: “If his offering is a burnt offering of the herd,” there is apparently no need for the verse to state this, as it was already stated earlier. Rather, this serves to exclude a tereifa from being brought as an offering.

verse.he: אִם־עֹלָה קׇרְבָּנוֹ מִן־הַבָּקָר זָכָר תָּמִים יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד יַקְרִיב אֹתוֹ לִרְצֹנוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: If your offering is a burnt offering from the herd, you shall make your offering a male without blemish. You shall bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, for acceptance in your behalf before GOD.

notes.dh: מן הבקר מן הבהמה מן הבקר ומן הצאן מן הבקר למטה
notes.he: אם עולה קרבנו מן הבקר שאין ללמוד שאינו צריך לכלום דהא כתיב מן הבקר לעיל האי דלמטה ודאי להוציא את הטרפה וקמא לנעבד. אלמא אתא קרא לטרפה:
notes.en: “From the animal,” “from the herd and from the flock,” “of the herd” below: “If his offering is a burnt offering of the herd,” for there is no need to state it, since “from the herd” is already written above. This lower one is certainly to exclude the tereifa, and the first one is for the worshipped animal. Evidently a verse comes for the tereifa.

notes.dh: כשהוא א' מן הבקר למטה שאין ת"ל
notes.he: דהוה יכול למימר אם עולה קרבנו בקר זכר תמים יקריבנו אלא מן להוציא את הטרפה:
notes.en: When it says “of the herd” below, there is no need to state it: since it could have said: “If his offering is a burnt offering, cattle, an unblemished male shall he offer”; rather, “of” comes to exclude the tereifa.

messages.text: In this case the derivation was necessary, as it might enter your mind to say: This statement, that a tereifa may not be sacrificed, applies where it became a tereifa and afterward was consecrated as an offering. But if it was consecrated and only afterward became a tereifa, I would say that it should be permitted to the Most High, despite the fact that it is prohibited in consumption. Consequently, the derivation from the verse is necessary.

notes.he: תרי קראי דאי ממשקה ישראל הוה אמינא למעוטי נטרפה ואחר כך הקדישה כו':
notes.en: It was necessary: two verses; for if there were only “the well-watered pastures of Israel,” I would say it excludes one that became a tereifa and afterward was consecrated, etc.

notes.he: להכי איצטריך מן הבקר אבל גבי מוקצה ונעבד תרי קראי ל"ל הא הקדישו ואח"כ הקצהו או עבדו לא מיתסר דלאו דידיה הוא ואין אדם אוסר דבר שאינו שלו אלא מדאיצטריך למעוטי לגבוה ודאי להדיוט מישרא שרי:
notes.en: I would say that it should be permitted: that is why “of the herd” was necessary. But with regard to set-aside and worshipped, why do I need two verses? If he consecrated it and afterward [someone] set it aside or worshipped it, it is not prohibited, since it is not his, and a person cannot render forbidden something that is not his. Rather, since a verse was needed to exclude them for the Most High, they are certainly permitted to an ordinary person.

notes.he: כלומר לעולם שמעינן ממשקה ישראל אסור לגבוה ואפ"ה איצטריך קרא למעוטי טרפה להיכא דהקדישה ואחר כך נטרפה ופירש רש"י אבל מוקצה ונעבד תרי קראי למה לי הרי הקדיש ואח"כ הקצהו או עבדו לא מיתסר דלאו דידיה הוא ואין אדם אוסר דבר שאינו שלו עכ"ל ולא נהירא דהא בפרק יוצא דופן (נדה מא.) גבי רובע ונרבע מצריך שתי קראי חד לבהמת קדשים וחד לבהמת חולין ומשכחת לה בקדשים קלים ואליבא דר' יוסי הגלילי לכן נראה לפרש דכי נמי שייך לומר כהאי גוונא במוקצה ונעבד ניחא דסוף סוף מהאי קרא דמן הבקר להוציא הנעבד לא שמעינן מיעוטא כי אם לחד גוונא להיכא דנעבדה ואחר כך הקדישה ואי ס"ד דאף להדיוט אסירי נכתביה גבי הדיוט ולגבוה שמעינן ליה ממשקה ישראל דאסור בהך גוונא דה"נ דאמר בטרפה דממשקה ישראל שמעינן איסור בנטרפה ואח"כ הקדישה לגבוה אלא ש"מ מדכתיב בפ' קרבנות דלהדיוט שרי ובפרק יוצא דופן (נדה מא.) מצריך קרא אחרינא לנעבד גופיה לגבוה להיכא דהקדישו ואחר כך נעבד שאם עלה ירד:
notes.en: It was necessary: that is, we always learn from “the well-watered pastures of Israel” that it is prohibited to the Most High, and even so a verse was needed to exclude a tereifa where it was consecrated and afterward became a tereifa. And Rashi explained: “But with regard to set-aside and worshipped, why do I need two verses? If he consecrated it and afterward set it aside or worshipped it, it is not prohibited, since it is not his, and a person cannot render forbidden something that is not his.” End of his words. And this is not clear, for in the chapter Yotzei Dofen (Nidda 41a), with regard to an animal that copulated with a person and one that was the object of bestiality, it requires two verses, one for a consecrated animal and one for a non-sacred animal, and the case is found with offerings of lesser sanctity, according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili [who holds that they are the owner’s property]. Therefore it seems right to explain: even if such a thing can be said with set-aside and worshipped, it is fine. For in the end, from this verse, “from the herd,” to exclude the worshipped, we learn an exclusion for only one case: where it was worshipped and afterward consecrated. And if it entered your mind that they are prohibited even to an ordinary person, let it be written with regard to the ordinary person, and for the Most High we would learn from “the well-watered pastures of Israel” that it is prohibited in this case, just as is said of the tereifa, that from “the well-watered pastures of Israel” we learn the prohibition for the Most High where it became a tereifa and afterward was consecrated. Rather, learn from the fact that it is written in the passage of offerings that it is permitted to an ordinary person. And in the chapter Yotzei Dofen (Nidda 41a) it requires another verse for the worshipped animal itself, for the Most High, where it was consecrated and afterward worshipped: that if it was brought up onto the altar, it is taken down.

notes.he: להוציא את הטרפה ולא מצי נפקא ממשקה ישראל דסד"א הני מילי דילפינן מינה כי נטרפה ואח"כ הקדישה דכי הקדישה לא הויא מותר לישראל אבל הקדישה ואח"כ נטרפה אימא תשתרי לגבוה כיון דבשעת הקדישה הוי מותר לישראל להכי איצטריך מן הבקר להוציא את הטרפה]:
notes.en: It was necessary: to exclude the tereifa, and it could not be derived from “the well-watered pastures of Israel,” for it might enter your mind that this applies only where it became a tereifa and afterward was consecrated, since when he consecrated it, it was not permitted to Israel. But if he consecrated it and afterward it became a tereifa, I would say it is permitted to the Most High, since at the time he consecrated it, it was permitted to Israel. That is why “of the herd” was necessary, to exclude the tereifa.

messages.text: But isn’t the halakha, that an animal which became a tereifa after it was consecrated is prohibited to be sacrificed, derived from here, a verse that deals with the animal tithe: “And all the tithe of the herd or the flock, whatsoever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be holy to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:32). The phrase: “Whatsoever passes under the rod,” indicates that the halakha of animal tithe applies only to an animal that can pass under the rod, excluding a tereifa, e.g., if its leg was cut above the knee, which cannot pass under the rod. From this paradigm case of a tereifa, the exception is expanded to apply to all tereifot.
messages.quote: it was consecrated and only afterward became a tereifa

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

notes.he: כגון שנחתכו רגליה מן הארכובה ולמעלה וכי הכא נפקא נטרפה ואחר כך הקדישה:
notes.en: Which cannot pass: for example, its legs were cut off from the knee upward. And [the Gemara asks whether] it is from here that [the case where] it became a tereifa and afterward was consecrated is derived.

notes.he: הקדישה ואח"כ נטרפה מהכא נפקא פרט לטרפה שאין עוברת כלומר אע"ג דקודם לכן לא הויא טרפה אלא לאחר שנכנסה לדיר נעשת טרפה שנשברה רגלה למעלה מן הארכובה אפי' הכי אינה עוברת אף הכא אע"פ דלא נטרפה אלא מאחר שהקדישה לא קרבה:
notes.en: But isn’t it derived from here: [the case where] he consecrated it and afterward it became a tereifa is derived from here, “excluding a tereifa, which cannot pass.” That is, even though before then it was not a tereifa, but only after it entered the pen did it become a tereifa, its leg having broken above the knee, even so it does not pass. So too here, even though it became a tereifa only after he consecrated it, it is not sacrificed.

messages.text: That derivation from animal tithe was also necessary, as it might enter your mind to say: This statement, that a tereifa may not be sacrificed, applies where it did not have a period of fitness to be sacrificed before it became a tereifa, e.g., where it was born a tereifa from its mother’s womb.
messages.quote: whatsoever passes under the rod

notes.he: ג' קראי דאי ממשקה ישראל ה"א דוקא היכא דנולדה טרפה דומיא דערלה וכלאי הכרם דכתיב בההוא קרא דכתיב ברישיה מן המאתים ואמרי' בפסחים (דף מח.) ממותר שתי מאות שנשתיירו בבור מכאן לערלה וכלאי הכרם שבטלין במאתים וכי היכי דערלה לא היתה לה שעת הכושר טרפה נמי לא נפקא לן מינה אלא דנולדה טרפה ולהכי איצטריכא כל אשר יעבור לנטרפה לאחר לידתה ואח"כ הקדישה ומן הבקר אתא להקדישה ואח"כ נטרפה:
notes.en: It was necessary: all three verses. For if there were only “the well-watered pastures of Israel,” I would say: specifically where it was born a tereifa, similar to orla and diverse kinds in a vineyard, which are derived from that verse. For at its beginning is written “out of two hundred,” and we say in Pesaḥim (48a): “From what remains of two hundred left in the pit”: from here [we learn that] orla and diverse kinds of the vineyard are nullified in two hundred. And just as orla never had a period of fitness, so too for the tereifa we would derive from it only one that was born a tereifa. That is why “whatsoever passes” was necessary, for one that became a tereifa after its birth and was afterward consecrated; and “of the herd” comes for one that was consecrated and afterward became a tereifa.

notes.he: כל אשר יעבר ואיצטריכו תלתיהו דאי ממשקה ישראל לחוד הוה אמינא הני מילי דלא היתה לו שעת הכושר דומיא דערלה וכלאי הכרם והיכי דמי כגון שנולדה טרפה ממעי אימה ההיא אסורה דלא היתה לה שעת הכושר אבל הכא דהיתה לה שעת הכושר דיצא' כו':
notes.en: That too was necessary: “whatsoever passes”; and all three were necessary. For if there were only “the well-watered pastures of Israel,” I would say this applies only where it never had a period of fitness, like orla and diverse kinds of the vineyard. And what are the circumstances? For example, where it was born a tereifa from its mother’s womb: that one is prohibited, since it never had a period of fitness. But here, where it had a period of fitness, since it emerged, etc.

messages.text: But in a case where it had a period of fitness and emerged into the air of the world and only afterward became a tereifa, I would say that it should be permitted to the Most High. Therefore, the phrase: “Whatsoever passes under the rod,” teaches us that even such an animal is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: להכי כתיב מן הבקר דלא אייתר ליה כל אשר יעבר [אלא] להיכא דהקדישה ואח"כ נטרפה דלא קרבה:
notes.en: I would say that it should be permitted: that is why “of the herd” is written [the printed text has a marginal suggestion: perhaps read “that even so it is prohibited”], and it is left over. “Whatsoever passes” is left over for the case where he consecrated it and afterward it became a tereifa: that it is not sacrificed.

messages.caption: Three verses that keep a tereifa off the altar, and the case each one is needed for, as Rashi assigns them.

messages.text: Mishna

And which is the case of an animal used as payment to a prostitute, which is prohibited as a sacrifice? It is the case of one who says to a prostitute: Here is this lamb as your fee. Even if they were one hundred lambs that he gave her, all of them are considered as payment to a prostitute and are prohibited.
And likewise, in the case of one who says to another: Here is this lamb and in return your maidservant will lie with my slave and engage in intercourse with him,
Its halakhic status is not that of payment to a prostitute,
Its halakhic status is that of payment to a prostitute.

notes.he: מתני' פלוגתא דרבי ורבנן מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: Mishna: the dispute of Rabbi [so Rashi’s text; the printed mishna has Rabbi Meir] and the Rabbis is explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: Gemara
The Master said in the mishna: And even if they were one hundred lambs, all of them are considered as payment to a prostitute, and are prohibited.
messages.quote: Even if they were one hundred lambs that he gave her, all of them are considered as payment

messages.text: What are the circumstances? If we say that this is referring to a prostitute who takes one hundred animals as payment for her services, it is obvious that all one hundred animals are prohibited, as what difference is it to me if she was paid one lamb or if she was paid one hundred lambs? What, then, is the novelty of the mishna here?

notes.dh: ל"א הכי דמי אי דהוי כו'
notes.he: מפרש כלישנא קמא:
notes.en: Another version: what are the circumstances? If it is, etc.: it explains as in the first version.

messages.text: No, it is necessary in a case where the prostitute takes one lamb as payment, and he gave her one hundred lambs. The mishna is teaching that in this case the extra lambs are not considered a gift. Rather, all the lambs are prohibited, as they all come from the source of a payment to a prostitute.

notes.he: והוא לא התנה לה אלא חד ונתן לה ב' וקמ"ל דאתנן ריבה לה וכולהו אתנן נינהו (ולא מתנה חד) שמתפסת אותו שהתנה עמה:
notes.en: Gemara: where she takes two [Rashi’s text reads “two”; the printed Gemara has “one” and “one hundred”]: and he had stipulated with her for only one, and gave her two; and it teaches us that he increased her payment, and all of them are payment (and not that one is a gift), since the one he stipulated with her draws [the others into its status].

notes.he: לא צריכא דשקלא אגרא חדא ויהב לה מאה סלקא דעתך אמינא אידך מתנה יהבינהו ניהלה ונישתרי קמ"ל דאסירי דכולהו מכח אתנן אתו דלשום עבירה יהבינהו לה:
notes.en: It is necessary only where she takes one fee and he gave her one hundred: it might enter your mind to say that he gave her the others as a gift, and they should be permitted. It teaches us that they are prohibited, since they all come by force of the payment, for he gave them to her for the sake of the transgression.

messages.text: If a man gave her an animal as payment but did not engage in intercourse with her, or if he engaged in intercourse with her but did not give her payment, her payment is permitted.
messages.lead: The Gemara continues to discuss the issue of payment to a prostitute. The Sages taught in a baraita:

messages.text: In a case where he gave her an animal as payment but did not engage in intercourse with her, do you call this her payment? It cannot be considered payment unless the act of intercourse was actually performed. And furthermore, in the second case, where he engaged in intercourse with her but did not give her payment, what did he give her that it is called a permitted payment?
messages.quote: gave her an animal as payment but did not engage in intercourse with her

messages.text: Rather, this is what the baraita is teaching: If he gave her payment and only afterward, when some time had elapsed, engaged in intercourse with her; or if he engaged in intercourse with her and only afterward gave her payment, in these two cases her payment is permitted.

notes.he: אלא הכי קתני נתן לה סתם אתננה מותר דאיכא למימר לשום מתנה יהב לה:
notes.en: Rather, this is what it teaches: he gave her [an animal] without specification; her payment is permitted, since one can say that he gave it to her as a gift.

messages.text:
But in the case where he gave her the lamb and later engaged in intercourse with her, let the status of payment to a prostitute take effect upon it retroactively.
Rabbi Elazar says:
messages.quote: If he gave her payment and only afterward, when some time had elapsed, engaged in intercourse with her

notes.he: הואיל ובשעת ביאה עדיין הטלה קיים וכיון שהוא בא עליה על שכר אותו טלה כל היכא דאיתיה חייל עליה אתנן דבשלמא בא עליה ואחר כך נתן לה טלה איכא למימר כיון דלא ייחדו בשעת ביאה לא מיתסר דמתנה בעלמא הוא:
notes.en: Let the status of payment take effect upon it retroactively: since at the time of intercourse the lamb is still extant, and since he engages in intercourse with her for the fee of that lamb, wherever it is, the status of payment takes effect upon it. Granted, where he engaged in intercourse with her and afterward gave her a lamb, one can say that since he did not designate it at the time of intercourse it is not prohibited, as it is a mere gift.

messages.text: …This is referring to a case where the prostitute first sacrificed the lamb as an offering, before she engaged in intercourse with the man who gave it her. In this case, the lamb is not considered payment to a prostitute.
messages.quote: let the status of payment to a prostitute take effect upon it retroactively

notes.he: קודם ביאה:
notes.en: Where she first sacrificed it: before intercourse.

notes.he: קודם שבא עליה להכי אתננה מותר:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar said: where she first sacrificed it, before he engaged in intercourse with her; that is why her payment is permitted.

messages.text: What are the circumstances? If we say that the man transferred ownership of the lamb to her immediately, and only afterward engaged in intercourse with her, it is obvious that this lamb is permitted to be sacrificed on the altar, as it belongs to her and up to that point the man had not yet engaged in intercourse with her. Therefore, the lamb is not considered payment at all.
messages.quote: where the prostitute first sacrificed the lamb

notes.he: והיכי דמי אי דאקנייה לה ניהליה בשעת שנתן לה:
notes.en: What are the circumstances? If he transferred it to her: at the time he gave it to her.

notes.he: דאפילו לא קדמה והקריבתו יהא מותר דלא חל עליה אתנן:
notes.en: It is obvious: that even had she not first sacrificed it, it would be permitted, since the status of payment does not take effect upon it.

notes.he: כשנתנו לה:
notes.en: For until then he had not engaged in intercourse with her: when he gave it to her.

messages.text: But rather, this must be referring to a case where he said to her: The lamb shall be acquired by you only at the time of intercourse, and yet she went ahead and sacrificed it beforehand. But in this case, can she legally sacrifice the lamb? The Merciful One states: “And when a man shall sanctify his house to be holy to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:14), which teaches that just as his house is in his possession, so too any item that a person wishes to sanctify must be in his possession. In this case, by contrast, the lamb does not belong to her until they engage in intercourse.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יַקְדִּשׁ אֶת־בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱרִיכוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כַּאֲשֶׁר יַעֲרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יָקוּם׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone who consecrates a house to GOD: The priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, as the priest assesses it, so it shall stand;

notes.dh: ואלא דאמר לה לא ניקני ליך עד שעת ביאה וקדמ' והקריבה
notes.he: ל"א דלא אקני לה היכי מציא מקרבא ליה ואיש כו':
notes.en: Rather, where he said to her: It shall not be acquired by you until the time of intercourse, and she went ahead and sacrificed it. Another version: since he did not transfer it to her, how can she sacrifice it? “And a man,” etc. [Leviticus 27:14].

messages.text: No, it is necessary in a case where he said to her: The lamb shall be acquired by you only at the time of intercourse, but if you need it in the meantime, acquire it for yourself from now. The baraita teaches that in such a case the lamb is permitted to be sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: הלכך ברשותה הוא ומציא לאקרוביה וכיון דאמר לה לא ליקני ליך עד שעת ביאה איצטריך לאשמועינן דמותר אם קדמה והקריבתו דסד"א אתנן הוי:
notes.en: And if you need it, take it from now: therefore it is in her possession and she can sacrifice it. And since he said to her: It shall not be acquired by you until the time of intercourse, it was necessary to teach us that it is permitted if she first sacrificed it, for it might enter your mind that it is payment.

notes.he: לא צריכא כגון דאמר לה לא נקני ליך עד שעת ביאה ואי מצטריך קודם או לאכול או להקריב ניקני ליך מעכשו דאע"ג כי אמר לה הכי לא ניקני ליך ודאי לשום אתנן יהבה ואפי' הכי כיון דאמר לה אי מצטרך ליך נקני ליך מעכשיו דהשתא הוה ברשותה דמציא מקרבה ליה אי קדמה והקריבתו מותר:
notes.en: It is necessary only where he said to her: It shall not be acquired by you until the time of intercourse, and if you need it before then, either to eat or to sacrifice, it shall be acquired by you from now. For even though, when he said to her “it shall not be acquired by you,” he certainly gave it as payment, even so, since he said to her “if you need it, it shall be acquired by you from now,” it is now in her possession and she can sacrifice it. If she first sacrificed it, it is permitted.

notes.he: ל"א אי מצטריך ליה אפקיה למאי דבעית:
notes.en: Another version: if you need it, take it out for whatever you wish.

messages.text: If she first consecrated the lamb before they engaged in intercourse but had not yet sacrificed it, what is the halakha?

Resolve the dilemma from that which Rabbi Elazar said, as Rabbi Elazar said above: The baraita is referring to a case where the prostitute first sacrificed the lamb as an offering. It can be inferred that it is not considered payment only if she actually sacrificed it, as the lamb is not extant at the time of intercourse. But if she merely consecrated it and had not yet sacrificed it, the lamb is prohibited, i.e., it is considered payment to a prostitute and therefore prohibited to be sacrificed upon the altar.
messages.quote: If she first consecrated the lamb

messages.text: Rav Oshaya raises this inference itself as a dilemma, as follows: May one infer from Rabbi Elazar’s statement that it is only if she sacrificed it before their intercourse and it is no longer in existence at the time of intercourse that it is permitted; but if she had merely consecrated it at the time of intercourse, the lamb is prohibited.

notes.he: פי' פשיטא ליה לרבי אלעזר הקריבתו אין הקדישתו לא או דלמא הקריבתו פשיטא ליה הקדישתו מספקא לי' תיקו:
notes.en: He raises the statement of Rabbi Elazar itself as a dilemma: meaning, was it obvious to Rabbi Elazar that if she sacrificed it, yes [it is permitted], but if she consecrated it, no? Or perhaps “she sacrificed it” was obvious to him, while “she consecrated it” was uncertain to him? It stands unresolved.

messages.text: Or perhaps one can argue otherwise: Since we learned in a mishna (Kiddushin 28b) that a declaration to the Most High, i.e., consecrating an item through speech, is equivalent to transferring an item to an ordinary person, therefore if she verbally consecrated the lamb before she engaged in intercourse with the man, it should be permitted to be sacrificed on the altar, as once she has dedicated the animal to God it no longer belongs to her. And all the more so the animal should be permitted if she actually sacrificed it.

notes.he: ולא מצי למיהדר כאילו מסרתו להדיוט:
notes.en: A declaration to the Most High: and he cannot retract, as though he had transferred it to an ordinary person.

messages.text: No answer is found, and the Gemara states that the dilemma shall stand unresolved.
§ The baraita teaches: If he engaged in intercourse with her and afterward gave her payment, her payment is permitted.
messages.quote: if he engaged in intercourse with her and only afterward gave her payment

messages.text: If he engaged in intercourse with her and afterward gave her payment, her payment is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar, and this is the case even if he gave it to her as much as twelve months later.
messages.lead: The Gemara asks: But isn’t it taught in another baraita:

messages.text: It is not difficult, as this second baraita is referring to a situation where he set aside a particular lamb and said to her before engaging in intercourse: Engage in intercourse with me for this lamb. In this case that lamb is considered hers as soon as they engage in intercourse, even if it was not actually given to her until much later. Therefore, it is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar as payment to a prostitute.
messages.quote: her payment is prohibited

notes.he: הואיל דיהביה בשעת ביאה חייל עליה אתנן מיד:
notes.en: For this lamb: since he gave it at the time of intercourse, the status of payment takes effect upon it immediately.

messages.text: By contrast, that first baraita is referring to a case where he said to her: Engage in intercourse with me for a lamb, without specification. Since he did not designate a lamb for her services at the time, the lamb he gives her later is not considered payment.

notes.he: דמשדר לה בתר הכי מתנה בעלמא הוא ואין אתנן אלא המיוחד בשעת ביאה:
notes.en: A lamb, without specification: what he sends her afterward is a mere gift, and payment is only what was designated at the time of intercourse.

messages.text: Even if he said to her: Engage in intercourse with me for this lamb, it should not be prohibited for sacrifice on the altar, as it lacks the formal act of acquisition of pulling, without which she does not acquire the animal.
The Gemara explains that this baraita is referring to a gentile prostitute, who does not acquire by pulling, as this method of acquisition cannot be performed by gentiles.
messages.quote: it lacks the formal act of acquisition of pulling

notes.he: הבעלי לי בטלה זה אפי' לא נתנו לה עד ג' שנים אסור. אבל הבעלי לי בטלה סתם ונתן לה לאחר שבא עליה מותר דאיכא למימר דהאי טלה כיון דלא יחדו לה אימר לשום מתנה יהביה לה. וכי אמר בטלה זה אמאי מיתסר והא מחוסר משיכה דלא משכתו הזונה ולא קנאתו וליהוי כי אמר לה בטלה סתם. בזונה עובדת כוכבים עסקינן דלא קניא במשיכה. ל"א דבמעות קניא העובדת כוכבים אף הכא נמי כיון דאמר לה בטלה זה ובא עליה מבעילתה קנאתו אע"ג דלא משכתו בדינו של עובדי כוכבים שקונה במעות שנותן בלא משיכה אף זו קנאתו בבעילה:
notes.en: Where he said to her: Engage in intercourse with me for this lamb: even if he did not give it to her until three years later [the printed Gemara: twelve months], it is prohibited. But where he said, Engage in intercourse with me for a lamb, without specification, and he gave it to her after he had engaged in intercourse with her, it is permitted, since one can say that this lamb, since he did not designate it for her, perhaps he gave it to her as a gift. And when he said, for this lamb, why is it prohibited? It lacks pulling, since the prostitute did not pull it and did not acquire it; let it be like when he said “for a lamb” without specification. We are dealing with a gentile prostitute, who does not acquire by pulling. Another version: since a gentile woman acquires with money, here too, since he said to her “for this lamb” and engaged in intercourse with her, she acquired it through her intercourse even though she did not pull it: by the law of gentiles, who acquire with money that they give without pulling, so too this one acquired it through the intercourse.

messages.text: And if you wish, say instead that this baraita is referring even to a Jewish prostitute, such as a case where the lamb is located in her courtyard, and she acquires it by means of her domain.

notes.he: משמע דלא מצינו אתנן אלא בכה"ג דקאי בחצירה וא"כ קשיא הא דאמר במרובה (ב"ק ע:) גבי אתנן אסרה תורה ואפי' בא על אמו דקאי עלה במיתה דאי תבעא ליה קמן לדינא לא א"ל זיל הב לה שהרי מתחייב בנפשו הוא וכיון דלא מצינו אתנן אלא דקאי בחצרה והיכי שייך למימר זיל הב לה הא תפסה בה ופר"י דכיון דאי לא הוה מוחזק בה לא אמר זיל הב לה אע"ג [דהשתא] דמטעם חצרה היא זוכה בה לא קרינא ליה אתנן אי לאו טעמא דמפרש התם כיון דקיהיב לה משום לצאת ידי שמים הוי אתנן ומורי הרמ"ר פי' דאין אנו צריכין לומר דבר זה דהא דמוקי ליה הכא דקאי בחצירה היינו משום דדחיק למצוא בא עליה ואח"כ נתן לה אבל הקנה לה קנין סודר כשתיבעלי לי תיקני ליך טלה זה בכל מקום שהוא קנוי ובהכי ניחא ההיא דמרובה (גז"ש) דאי תבעא ליה קמן לדינא לא אמרינן ליה זיל הב לה:
notes.en: Such as where it is standing in her courtyard: this implies that we find payment only in such a case, where it is standing in her courtyard. If so, there is a difficulty with what is said in Merubbe (Bava Kamma 70b) with regard to payment: the Torah prohibited payment even where he engaged in intercourse with his mother, where he is liable to death [and so exempt from monetary payment], since if she summoned him before us to judgment we would not say to him: Go, give it to her, for he is liable with his life. Now, since we find payment only where it is standing in her courtyard, how does it apply to say “Go, give it to her”? She has already seized it! And the Ri explained: since, had she not been in possession of it, we would not say to him “Go, give it to her,” then even though she now acquires it by virtue of her courtyard, we would not call it payment, were it not for the reason explained there: since he gives it to her in order to fulfill his obligation in the eyes of Heaven, it is payment. And my teacher the Ramar explained that we need not say this. The reason the Gemara establishes it here as standing in her courtyard is that it is hard to find [a case of] “he engaged in intercourse with her and afterward gave her”; but if he transferred it to her with a kinyan sudar [acquisition by means of a cloth]: When you have intercourse with me, this lamb shall be acquired by you, it is acquired wherever it is. And with this the passage in Merubbe is fine: if she summoned him before us to judgment, we would not say to him, Go, give it to her.

notes.he: ומשכחת לה דמן שעה שבא עליה קנייה כי אמר בטלה זה וכגון דאוקמוה בחצרה דחצירו של אדם קונה לו:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: even a Jewish prostitute. And it is found that from the time he engaged in intercourse with her she acquired it, when he said “for this lamb,” for example, where they stationed it in her courtyard, for a person’s courtyard acquires for him.

messages.text: If the lamb is in her courtyard, why does the baraita state that he gave it to her after twelve months? He gave it to her at the outset, before they engaged in intercourse, and she acquired it at that time via her courtyard.
messages.quote: the lamb is located in her courtyard

notes.he: דהואיל וקאי בחצרה קניא ליה בשעת ביאה מיד ואמאי קרי ליה ואח"כ נתן ועוד פשיטא דאסור:
notes.en: But he gave it to her at the outset: since it is standing in her courtyard, she acquires it immediately at the time of intercourse. So why does it call it “and afterward he gave”? And furthermore, it is obvious that it is prohibited.

notes.he: (אי) [הא] יהבה לה מעיקרא הוא קודם ביאה כי אוקמוה בחצירה ואמאי קא מיירי בבא עליה ואח"כ נתן לה:
notes.en: If so, he gave it to her at the outset, before intercourse, when they stationed it in her courtyard. So why is it speaking of “he engaged in intercourse with her and afterward gave her”?

messages.text: The baraita is referring to a case where he established the lamb for her as designated payment, and said to her: If by such and such a day I give you money as your payment, all is well, and you will return the lamb to me. And if I have not given you money by that date, then the lamb itself shall be your payment.

notes.dh: עד יום פלוני משקלין לך כך וכך ואי לא שקלי ליה
notes.he: הלכך כי מטו ולא יהיב לה זוזי איגלאי מילתא [דדידה הואי בשע'] ביאה ומיהו אח"כ הוא דהא לא הוי דידה עד דמטי יום פלוני ואיצטריך לאשמועינן דאסור:
notes.en: By such and such a day I will pay you such and such, and if I do not pay: therefore, when the day arrives and he has not given her money, it becomes clear [that it was hers at the time] of intercourse. But it is [called given] afterward, since it was not hers until such and such a day arrived; and it was necessary to teach us that it is prohibited.

notes.he: האי טלה אפותיקי ואמר לה אי עד יום פלוני (לא) יהיבנא לך זוזי דאתננך מוטב ואי לאו כוליה טלה טלי באתנניך הילכך כיון דשויא לה אפותיקי קנאתו ולא לגמרי עד אם יעבור הזמן הלכך הוי נמי כמו שבא עליה ואח"כ נתן לה:
notes.en: Rather, where he made it for her: this lamb, a security [apotiki], and said to her: If by such and such a day I give you money for your payment, well and good; and if not, take the whole lamb as your payment. Therefore, since he made it a security for her, she acquired it, but not fully until the time passes; therefore it too is like “he engaged in intercourse with her and afterward gave her.”

notes.he: ל"א האי דאוקמא דקאי בחצירו נתן לה ואח"כ בא עליה אלא כגון דאתפסיה רועה ניהלה במשיכה ואח"כ בא לידו של רבו ולא נתנה לה עד לאחר ביאה:
notes.en: Another version: where it is established as standing in [her] courtyard, he gave it to her and afterward engaged in intercourse with her. Rather, for example, where a shepherd handed it over to her by pulling, and afterward it came into his master’s hands, and he did not give it to her until after intercourse.

messages.text: Both the payment given for intercourse of a male with a male, and the payment given for intercourse with any of those with whom relations are forbidden, have the status of payment to a prostitute and are therefore prohibited. Such an animal may not be used as a sacrifice, except for payment to one’s menstruating wife.
messages.lead: § The Gemara continues to discuss the definition of payment to a prostitute that is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: שבא על הזכר ונתן לו אתנן אסור להקרבה:
notes.en: The payment of a male: one who engaged in intercourse with a male and gave him payment; it is prohibited for sacrifice.

messages.text: What is the reason that payment to one’s menstruating wife is permitted? The reason is that it is written “prostitute,” with regard to this prohibition: “You shall not bring the hire of a prostitute or the price of a dog into the House of the Lord your God, for both of them are an abomination to the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 23:19), and this woman, his menstruating wife, is not a prostitute.
messages.quote: except for payment to one’s menstruating wife

verse.he: לֹא־תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְכׇל־נֶדֶר כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: You shall not bring the fee of a whore or the pay of a dog into the house of the ETERNAL your God in fulfillment of any vow, for both are abhorrent to the ETERNAL your God.

messages.text: Even the payment for intercourse with one’s menstruating wife is considered payment to a prostitute and is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar.

What is the reason? It is written “abomination” in the above verse, and this intercourse with one’s menstruating wife is also called an abomination, as it is written with regard to those with whom relations are forbidden, including a menstruating wife: “For whoever shall do any of these abominations” (Leviticus 18:29).
messages.quote: Even the payment for intercourse with one’s menstruating wife

verse.he: כִּי כׇּל־אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה מִכֹּל הַתּוֹעֵבֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְנִכְרְתוּ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הָעֹשֹׂת מִקֶּרֶב עַמָּם׃
verse.en: All who do any of those abhorrent things—such persons shall be cut off from among their people.

notes.he: כי תועבת ה' אלהיך גם שניהם והאי נמי תועבה הוא דנדה כתיבא גבי עריות ואכולהי כתיב את כל התועבות האלה:
notes.en: “Abomination” is written: “For both of them are an abomination to the Lord your God.” And this too is an abomination, for the menstruating woman is written among the forbidden relations, and of all of them it is written: “All these abominations.”

messages.text: And according to the opinion of Levi as well, isn’t it written “prostitute,” with regard to this payment, and one’s wife is not a prostitute.

notes.he: (ואי) [והא] אשתו נדה תועבה היא דכתיבא גבי עריות וכתב בסיפיה כי כל אשר יעשה מכל התועבות האלה. וללוי דמרבי אשתו נדה הא כתב זונה ואשתו נדה לאו זונה:
notes.en: What is the reason? “For it is an abomination” is written, and his menstruating wife is an abomination, since she is written among the forbidden relations, and at the end of it is written: “For whoever shall do any of these abominations.” And according to Levi, who includes his menstruating wife: but “prostitute” is written, and his menstruating wife is not a prostitute.

messages.text: That term teaches that this prohibition applies only to a female prostitute who receives payment from a man, and not to a male prostitute who is paid by a woman.
messages.lead: The Gemara answers that Levi could have said to you:

notes.he: דאם נתנה לו היא באתנן מותר:
notes.en: And not a male prostitute: for if she gave him payment, it is permitted.

notes.he: (אי) [ורב] קסבר דהאי [זונה] להכי אתא דאתנן זונה אסורה ולא אתנן זונה אם נתנה היא לו אתנן אינו אסור להקרבה:
notes.en: And Rav [the printed text emends to “and Rav”; in the Gemara this answer is given for Levi] holds that this “prostitute” comes for this: that the payment of a female prostitute is prohibited, but not the payment of a male prostitute; if she gave him payment, it is not prohibited for sacrifice.

messages.text: And according to the opinion of Rav, who derives from the word “prostitute” that one’s menstruating wife is excluded, from where does he derive that halakha that the prohibition applies only to a female prostitute who receives payment from a man and not to a male prostitute who receives payment from a woman?
Rav derives it from that which Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said. As it is taught in a baraita:

The only payment to a prostitute that is prohibited for sacrifice on the altar is any payment given to one with whom intercourse is a transgression for him and is never permitted. But with regard to an animal given as payment by a husband to his menstruating wife for intercourse, and payment that he gave to a prostitute as a fee for her neglect of other paid labor that she could have been performing at that time, but not as payment for intercourse, and an animal that a woman gave him as his payment, all these are permitted to be sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: שאין לך צד היתר בה אבל אשתו נדה דמותר בה לאחר זמן או שנתן לה לזונה שכר פקיעתה שכר מה שבטלה ממלאכתה ולא שכר ביאה:
notes.en: Who come to him through transgression: in whom there is no aspect of permission. But his menstruating wife, who is permitted to him after a time, or where he gave a prostitute a fee for her neglect, payment for the time she was idle from her work and not payment for intercourse [these are permitted].

notes.he: לא שכר עבירה אלא שכר שבטלה באותה שעה ממלאכתה כולן מותרין]:
notes.en: Or where he gave her a fee for her neglect: not payment for the transgression, but payment for her being idle at that time from her work; all of these are permitted.

messages.text: Even though there is no proof for the matter, that an animal given by a woman to a man for services rendered is not considered payment to a prostitute, nevertheless there is an allusion to the matter in the verses: “To all prostitutes gifts are given; but you have given your gifts to all your lovers, and have bribed them to come unto you from every side in your harlotries. And the contrary is in you from other women, in that you did solicit to prostitution, and you were not solicited; and in that you gave hire, and no hire is given to you, thus you are contrary” (Ezekiel 16:33–34). This indicates that it is contrary to the manner of prostitution for the woman to pay the man to engage in intercourse with her.

verse.he: לְכׇל־זֹנוֹת יִתְּנוּ־נֵדֶה וְאַתְּ נָתַתְּ אֶת־נְדָנַיִךְ לְכׇל־מְאַהֲבַיִךְ וַתִּשְׁחֳדִי אוֹתָם לָבוֹא אֵלַיִךְ מִסָּבִיב בְּתַזְנוּתָיִךְ׃ וַיְהִי־בָךְ הֵפֶךְ מִן־הַנָּשִׁים בְּתַזְנוּתַיִךְ וְאַחֲרַיִךְ לֹא זוּנָּה וּבְתִתֵּךְ אֶתְנָן וְאֶתְנַן לֹא נִתַּן־לָךְ וַתְּהִי לְהֶפֶךְ׃
verse.en: Gifts are made to all prostitutes, but you made gifts to all your lovers, and bribed them to come to you from every quarter for your whoring. You were the opposite of other women: you solicited instead of being solicited; you paid fees instead of being paid fees. Thus you were just the opposite!

notes.he: דלישתרי להקרבה זכר לדבר דלא הוי אתנן מה שהיא נותנת לו מדכתיב ותהי להפך:
notes.en: And even though there is no proof for the matter: that it should be permitted for sacrifice, there is an allusion to the matter that what she gives him is not payment, from what is written: “Thus you are contrary.”

notes.he: שאתנן זונה קרוי אתנן זכר לדבר שנאמר ובתתך אתנן וקאמר דכולן מותרין:
notes.en: And even though there is no proof for the matter: there is an allusion to the matter that a prostitute’s payment is called payment, as it is said: “And in that you gave hire.” And he says that all of these are permitted.

messages.text: And Rav, this word “abomination” (Deuteronomy 23:19), from which Levi derives his ruling that an animal given by a husband for intercourse with his menstruating wife is considered payment to a prostitute, what does he do with it?
Rav requires this word for that which Abaye said.
With regard to a gentile prostitute, her payment is prohibited.

What is the reason? It is written here, with regard to payment to a prostitute, “abomination,” and it is written there, with regard to forbidden sexual relations: “For whoever shall do any of these abominations” (Leviticus 18:29). Just as there the verse is referring to those with whom relations are forbidden and with whom betrothal does not take effect, so too, the prohibition of payment to a prostitute is referring to a woman with whom betrothal does not take effect, including a gentile.

verse.he: כִּי כׇּל־אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה מִכֹּל הַתּוֹעֵבֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְנִכְרְתוּ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הָעֹשֹׂת מִקֶּרֶב עַמָּם׃
verse.en: All who do any of those abhorrent things—such persons shall be cut off from among their people.

notes.dh: [ורב האי תועבה דדריש ליה לוי לאתנן לאשתו נדה מאי עביד ליה מיבעי ליה כו'
notes.he: ילפה תועבה תועבה מעריות כתיב גבי אתנן כי תועבה היא וכתי' בעריות מכל התועבות. יצא עובדת כוכבים שאין זרעו מיוחס אחריו כדאמרי' ואין בנך הבא מן העובדת כוכבים קרוי בנך אלא בנה]:
notes.en: And Rav, this “abomination” that Levi expounds for payment to his menstruating wife, what does he do with it? He requires it, etc. He derives “abomination,” “abomination” from forbidden relations: it is written with regard to payment “for it is an abomination,” and it is written with regard to forbidden relations “of all these abominations.” Excluded is a gentile woman, whose offspring are not attributed to him, as we say: Your son from a gentile woman is not called your son, but her son.

messages.text: And with regard to a gentile prostitute: A priest who engaged in intercourse with her is not flogged for engaging in intercourse with her due to the prohibition with regard to priests: “They shall not take a woman who is a prostitute” (Leviticus 21:7).

verse.he: אִשָּׁה זֹנָה וַחֲלָלָה לֹא יִקָּחוּ וְאִשָּׁה גְּרוּשָׁה מֵאִישָׁהּ לֹא יִקָּחוּ כִּי־קָדֹשׁ הוּא לֵאלֹהָיו׃
verse.en: They shall not marry a woman defiled by prostitution, nor shall they marry one divorced from her husband. For they are holy to their God

messages.text: What is the reason? It is because the verse states: “And he shall not profane his seed among his people” (Leviticus 21:15). This verse indicates that the prohibition of profaning his seed applies only to a priest who engages in intercourse with a woman whose offspring are attributed to him, i.e., a Jew, where the lineage of the children is determined by the identity of the father. This excludes a priest who engaged in intercourse with a gentile woman, whose offspring are not attributed to him, but to her, as their child is a gentile.

verse.he: וְלֹא־יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ בְּעַמָּיו כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה מְקַדְּשׁוֹ׃ {ס}
verse.en: that he may not profane his offspring among his kin, for I GOD have sanctified him.

notes.dh: עובדת כוכבים אין זרעו מיוחס אחריו
notes.he: דלא מיקרי זרעו אלא בנה כדאמרינן ביבמות (דף כג.) בנך הבא מישראלית קרוי בנך ואין בנך הבא מן העובדת כוכבים קרוי בנך אלא בנה:
notes.en: A gentile woman, whose offspring are not attributed to him: for the child is not called his offspring but her son, as we say in Yevamot (23a): Your son from a Jewish woman is called your son, but your son from a gentile woman is not called your son, but her son.

messages.text: With regard to one who engages in intercourse with an unmarried Jewish prostitute, her payment is permitted to be sacrificed on the altar. What is the reason? It is that betrothal takes effect with her, and payment is prohibited only in the case of a prostitute with whom betrothal is ineffective.

And a priest who engaged in intercourse with her is flogged due to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with a prostitute. What is the reason? It is because his offspring from this relationship are attributed to him.

With regard to both this, a gentile prostitute, and that, a Jewish prostitute, her payment is prohibited, and a priest who engaged in intercourse with her is flogged due to the prohibition against having intercourse with a prostitute. What is the reason? It is that these two cases are derived from one another: Just as engaging in intercourse with a Jewish prostitute is forbidden to a priest by a prohibition, so too his engaging in intercourse with a gentile prostitute is forbidden by a prohibition. And just as payment to a gentile prostitute is prohibited, so too payment to a Jewish prostitute is prohibited.

notes.he: במה מצינו:
notes.en: What is the reason? They are derived from one another: by [the method of] ma matzinu [an analogy from what we have found].

notes.dh: ורבא אמר אחת זו ואחת זו אתננה אסור וכהן הבא עליה לוקה משום זונה
notes.he: וקשיא א"כ מה גזרו ב"ד של חשמונאי דגזרו הבא על העובדת כוכבים חייב משום נשג"ז הא אמר הכא דעובדת כוכבים זונה דאורייתא היא וי"ל דרבא סבירא ליה כמ"ד נשג"א אבל משום זונה לקי דאורייתא וא"ת לאביי דאמר כהן הבא על העובדת כוכבים אינו לוקה משום זונה הא תנן בפרק הבא על יבמתו (יבמות נט: וסא:) אין זונה אלא גיורת ושנבעלה בעילת זנות אלמא דעובדת כוכבים היא זונה וי"ל דבנתגיירה ודאי היא זונה אבל בעודה עובדת כוכבים לא הוי זונה:
notes.en: And Rava says: both this and that, her payment is prohibited, and a priest who engaged in intercourse with her is flogged on account of a prostitute: this is difficult. If so, what did the court of the Hasmoneans decree? For they decreed that one who has intercourse with a gentile woman is liable on account of NaShGaZ [menstruating woman, maidservant, gentile, prostitute], yet here it says that a gentile woman is a prostitute by Torah law! One may say that Rava holds like the one who says NaShGA [menstruating woman, maidservant, gentile, married woman], but on account of a prostitute he is flogged by Torah law. And if you say: according to Abaye, who said that a priest who has intercourse with a gentile woman is not flogged on account of a prostitute, but we learned in the chapter HaBa al Yevimto (Yevamot 59b and 61a): “A prostitute is only a convert, and one who had licentious intercourse,” evidently a gentile woman is a prostitute! One may say: once she has converted, she is certainly a prostitute; but while she is still a gentile, she is not a prostitute.

notes.he: וכהן הבא עליה אפי' על עובדת כוכבים לוקה משום זונה. דילפי מהדדי מה זונה ישראל בלאו דכתב לא יחלל אף עובדת כוכבים נמי בלאו ומה אתנן עובדת כוכבי' אסור דהא לא תפסי קידושי אף דזונה ישראל אסור אע"ג דתפסי בה קידושי דהא ילפן אהדדי:
notes.en: And Rava says, etc.: and a priest who has intercourse with her, even with a gentile woman, is flogged on account of a prostitute, since they are derived from one another. Just as a Jewish prostitute is by a prohibition, as it is written “he shall not profane,” so too a gentile woman by a prohibition; and just as payment to a gentile woman is prohibited, since betrothal does not take effect with her, so too payment to a Jewish prostitute is prohibited even though betrothal takes effect with her, since they are derived from one another.

messages.caption: Abaye and Rava on a gentile and a Jewish prostitute: is her payment prohibited for the altar, and is a priest flogged?

messages.text: With regard to both a gentile prostitute and a Jewish prostitute, their payment is prohibited.
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection to the opinion of Abaye from a baraita:

notes.dh: גירסא ראשונה מיתיבי אחת זונה ואחת עובדת כוכבים
notes.he: קס"ד דה"ק אחת זונה ישראלית כגון שנבעלה לאחד מחייבי כריתות שהיתה זונה כבר הוי אתנן לכל אדם אפי' היא נשכרת עתה למותר לה אי נמי זונה שהיתה מופקרת הויא אתנן והיינו כרבא ותיובתא דאביי דיליף תועבה תועבה דאין אתנן אלא לעריות שאין קדושין תופסין בה ופריך הא דקתני סיפא כגון אלמנה לכ"ג כו' והני קדושין תופסין בה ומשני הא מני ר' אלעזר היא דאמר פנוי הבא על הפנויה עשאה זונה ולדידיה הוי אתנן בכל הבעילות שאינו לאשתו גמורה אבל לרבנן לעולם אימא לך דלא הויא אתנן אלא מביאה דלא תפסי בה קדושין וצ"ע מנא ליה לאביי הא דלא יליף רבי אלעזר תועבה תועבה לומר דלא הויא אתנן אלא לאותן שאין קדושין תופסין בה כמו לרבנן ויש לומר דכיון דאית ליה לר' אלעזר דכל ביאה הויא זונה אלמא מחמיר הוא בזונה יותר משאר תנאים הכא נמי אמר לגבי אתנן דמחמיר יותר משאר תנאים והויא אתנן בכל ביאה ואפי' מפנוי לפנויה ופריך אי ר' אלעזר מאי איריא אלמנה ניתני פנויה ומשני סלקא דעתך אמינא הואיל ובנין אב הוא לא ליתסרו ופירש רש"י הואיל ובנין אב הוא ללמוד שאין אתנן אסור אלא בפנוי ופנויה אבל מאלמנה לכהן גדול דאסורה ליה כבר לא הויא אתנן קמשמע לן זה ל' רש"י וקשה להבין ורבינו נתנאל פירש הואיל ובנין אב הוא דמשוי דין אתנן לדין איסורא דכהן מזונה כדאמרינן דכל ביאה שהיא אסורה לכהן הוי אתנן ואפי' מפנוי אפנויה ה"נ ילפינן דין אתנן מכהן דומיא דזונה דכהן הוי אתנן כלומר שאין בה שם אחר אבל מאלמנה לכ"ג דאין בה איסור משום זונה אלא שם אחר יש בה לא הויא אתנן קמ"ל דבהאי נמי הויא אתנן ועוד יש גירסא אחרת בספרים מיתיבי כו' עד הא דקתני בסיפא כו' ומשני הא מני ר"ע היא דאמר אין קדושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין והא קמ"ל דכל זונה דומיא דאלמנה לכ"ג לא תפסי בה קדושין וצ"ע מאי הוי קשיא ליה ומאי הוצרך לאגמורי למילתיה הא קמ"ל הא תירץ שפיר כיון דאמר הא מני ר"ע היא וי"ל דהוה קשיא ליה הא דקתני סיפא כגון אלמנה לכ"ג אמאי איצטריך למיתני הכי ולאוקומי כר"ע לא ליתני אלא רישא אחת זונה ישראלית ותיתי ככ"ע ובכל ביאה דהוה בה זונה הויא אתנן לרבנן בחייבי כריתות ולר"ע בחייבי לאוין ולהכי אגמריה למילתיה הא קמ"ל דומיא דאלמנה לכ"ג דאי לא הוה תני אלא רישא אחת זונה ישראלית איכא למיטעי ולומר דהויא זונה כבר כגון שנבעלה לחייבי כריתות א"נ זונה מופקרת הויא זונה לגבי אתנן אפילו היא נשכרת ונבעלת למותר לה להכי תנא סיפא כגון אלמנה לכ"ג לאשמועינן דלא הויא אתנן אלא מביאה דלא תפסי בה קדושין דומיא דאלמנה לכהן גדול לר"ע ולרבא. דאמר אפי' תפסי בה קדושין הויא אתנן בין שהיתה זונה כבר כגון שנבעלה כבר לחייבי כריתות אי נמי כגון זונה מופקרת מאי שנא דקתני כגון אלמנה לכה"ג ומשני דומיא דאלמנה מה אלמנה סתמא לא לקי עד דמתרו בה אף זונה עד דאמר לה היליכי אתנן ואז הוי אתנן דזנות הוא כיון שמזכיר לה לשון אתנן לא הויא אתנן ולאפוקי מדר' אלעזר דאמר פנוי הבא על הפנויה עשאה זונה ולדידיה אפי' בחדא זימנא הויא זונה אפי' בסתמא הויא זונה אבל היכא דהויא זונה מעיקרא אתננה אסור אפילו בסתמא דמופקרת היא ואתנן זונה מיקרי כפרש"י ודוחק הוא לפרש היכא אשכחנא דבסתמא לא הויא אתנן לרבנן (היא) אי בפנויה הא לית להו דהויא אתנן כלל אפי' אמר לה הילך אתנן ואי בזונה כבר כגון שנבעלה לחייבי כריתות או מופקרת הא אמרו דאפי' בסתמא הויא אתנן לכ"נ לפרש אף זונה עד דאמר לה הילך אתנן כלומר אי נתן אתנן לזונה שנבעלה כבר לחייבי כריתות או לזונה שהיא מופקרת לא הויא אתנן אא"כ מפרש לה בהדיא הילך טלה זה באתננך אבל נתן לה בסתמא ולא פירש לא הויא אתנן ולאפוקי מדר' אלעזר דלדידיה דמחמיר בזונה כל כך דאפילו פנוי הבא על הפנויה עשאה זונה אפי' בסתמא נמי הוי אתנן אבל היכא דזונה היא מעיקרא פירוש לרבנן נמי היכא דהויא זונה בההיא ביאה שהוא נותן לה האתנן כגון אם הוא נותן לאחותו או לאחד מחייבי כריתות אפי' בסתמא הויא אתנן כיון דבאותה ביאה שויא זונה כדאמר לר' אלעזר דמשום דמשוי לה זונה אפי' בפנוי הבא על הפנויה הויא אתנן אפי' בסתמא היכא דהיא נעשית זונה באותה ביאה אבל היכא דנעשית זונה כבר ובא אחר דתפיס בה קידושין ונתן לה אתנן לא הויא אתנן בסתמא אא"כ פירש בהדיא הילך טלה זה באתננך:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot sets out two readings of this passage.
